q: In double entry bookkeeping, every transaction
o: is recorded only in the cash book
is recorded only on the credit side
e: One account is debited and another is credited with the same amount.

q: Goods bought on credit are recorded by debiting
e: Purchases is debited and the supplier's (creditor's) account is credited.

q: The book in which cash receipts and payments are first recorded is the
e: The cash book is both a book of original entry and a ledger account.

q: Which of these is a current asset?
e: Debtors will pay within a year, so they are current assets.

q: Gross profit is calculated as
o: sales minus cost of goods sold
e: Gross profit is found in the trading account.

q: Net profit is gross profit
e: Expenses are deducted in the profit and loss account.

q: A trial balance is prepared to
o: show the value of the business
check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger accounts
e: If debits equal credits, the ledger is arithmetically correct.

q: Depreciation is the
o: increase in the value of an asset
allocation of the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life
cash set aside to replace an asset
profit made on selling an asset
e: It spreads the cost over the years the asset is used.

q: A machine costs N100,000, has a scrap value of N10,000 and a life of 5 years. Straight-line depreciation per year is
Which of these is capital expenditure?
e: It gives benefit over several years and is added to fixed assets.

q: Which of these is revenue expenditure?
e: Day-to-day running costs are revenue expenditure.

q: Bad debts are
o: debts that cannot be collected from debtors
e: They are written off as an expense.

q: A provision for doubtful debts is made because of the concept of
e: Prudence means not overstating profits or assets.

q: The concept that treats the business and its owner as separate is the
e: The owner's private affairs are kept out of the business books.

q: Closing stock is valued at
o: the higher of cost and selling price
the lower of cost and net realisable value
e: This follows the prudence concept.

q: Drawings are
o: money or goods taken by the owner for personal use
e: Drawings reduce the owner's capital.

q: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to
o: explain differences between the cash book and the bank statement
calculate the profit of the business
e: It reconciles the two balances.

q: A cheque that has been issued but not yet paid by the bank is
e: It causes the bank statement to show a higher balance than the cash book.

q: The journal is used to record
o: opening entries and corrections of errors
e: It is the book of original entry for items with no other book.

q: The sales returns book records
e: It is also called the returns inwards book.

q: The current ratio is
o: current assets divided by current liabilities
current liabilities divided by current assets
e: It measures a firm's ability to pay short-term debts.

q: Liabilities due for payment within one year are
e: Examples are creditors and bank overdraft.

q: Goodwill is an example of
e: It has no physical form.

q: Which account normally has a credit balance?
e: Capital is what the business owes the owner.

q: Cash received is entered on the
o: debit side of the cash account
credit side of the cash account
debit side of the capital account
credit side of the sales account
e: Cash is an asset, and an asset increases on the debit side.

q: Accrued expenses are expenses that have been
e: They are shown as current liabilities.

q: Prepaid expenses are expenses
o: owed at the end of the year
e: They are shown as current assets.

q: The trading account is prepared to find the
e: It matches sales with the cost of goods sold.

q: The petty cash book uses the imprest system, which means
o: a fixed float is refilled to its original amount
all cash goes to the bank daily
e: The cashier gets back exactly what was spent.

q: If a partnership agreement says nothing about sharing profits, they are shared
e: That is the rule under partnership law.

q: The sales ledger control account contains the totals of
e: It checks the accuracy of the debtors ledger.

q: The purchases day book records
e: Cash purchases go in the cash book.

q: Dividends are paid to shareholders out of
e: Dividends are a share of the company's profit.

q: Cost of goods sold equals
o: opening stock minus purchases plus closing stock
opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock
e: It shows the cost of the goods actually sold.

q: Debenture holders are
e: They lend money and receive interest.

q: A suspense account is used to
o: hold a difference in the trial balance until the error is found
e: It is cleared once the errors are corrected.

q: Under the realisation concept, revenue is recognised when
o: goods are delivered or services are performed
e: Revenue is earned at the point of sale, not before.

q: Stock turnover is calculated as
o: cost of goods sold divided by average stock
e: It shows how many times stock is sold and replaced.

q: Carriage inwards is added to
o: expenses in the profit and loss account
e: It is a cost of bringing goods to the business, so it forms part of the cost of goods.

q: Carriage outwards is treated as
o: a selling expense in the profit and loss account
e: It is the cost of delivering goods to customers.

q: Discount allowed is
e: It is given to customers who pay early.

q: Discount received is
e: It is given by suppliers when the business pays early.

q: Opening stock plus purchases, less closing stock, gives the
e: This is the cost of the goods actually sold in the period.

q: The gross profit margin is calculated as
o: gross profit divided by purchases, multiplied by 100
gross profit divided by sales, multiplied by 100
net profit divided by sales, multiplied by 100
sales divided by gross profit, multiplied by 100
e: It shows the profit on each naira of sales before expenses.

A van bought for N500,000 is depreciated at 20% on the reducing balance. The depreciation in the second year is
e: First year N100,000; the book value N400,000 x 20% = N80,000.

q: Working capital is
e: It shows the funds available for day-to-day running.

q: The acid test (quick) ratio leaves out
e: Stock cannot be turned into cash quickly.

q: A statement of affairs is used to find the capital of a business that keeps
e: Capital is found by subtracting liabilities from assets.

q: The receipts and payments account of a club is
o: a summary of its cash book
e: It lists cash received and paid in the period.

q: In a non-profit organisation, the excess of income over expenditure is called
e: It is added to the accumulated fund.

q: The accumulated fund of a club is similar to
e: It is the net worth of the club.

q: In a partnership, a partner's share of profit is shown in the
e: Interest on capital, salaries and shares of profit are shown there.

q: The authorised share capital of a company is
o: the maximum share capital it may issue
its profits kept in the business
e: It is stated in the memorandum of association.

q: Preference shareholders are paid
o: a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders
e: They are given priority for dividends.

q: The owners of a limited company are the
e: They share in the profits and risks.

q: Debenture interest is
o: paid out of profit after tax
an expense charged before arriving at profit
e: Debentures are loans, so their interest is a cost.

q: A trial balance that agrees does NOT prove
o: that the ledger totals are added correctly
that there are no errors in the books
e: Some errors do not affect the totals.

q: If a transaction is left out of the books altogether, this is an error of
e: The trial balance still balances.

q: If a payment is posted to the wrong customer's account, this is an error of
e: The account is of the right class but wrong.

q: Recording the purchase of a machine as a purchase of goods is an error of
e: Items were put in the wrong class of account.

q: The purchases ledger control account contains the totals of
e: It checks the personal accounts of suppliers.

q: A bank overdraft is shown as a
e: It is repayable on demand.

q: A contra entry in the cash book is used when
o: cash is paid into the bank, or drawn from it
e: It appears on both the cash and bank sides.

q: The accounting concept that assumes a business will continue in operation is the
e: It lets assets be valued as for continuing use.

q: Using the same accounting methods from year to year follows the concept of
e: It makes results from different years comparable.

q: The concept that expenses are matched with the revenue they helped to earn is the
e: It is also called the accrual concept.

q: Prime cost in a manufacturing account is made up of
o: direct materials, direct labour and direct expenses
e: It is the total of direct costs of production.
